advances:
Adds an exact diagonal-rail gate inside the retained maximum-chord
hard interval of accepted fact `3c17eb0b21eeb63c`.  More
fundamentally, it proves that the purported \(Q_{123}\)-side loss of
the two active \(A_2\)-traces cannot occur under the exact support:
the complete row-1 trace belongs to \(\overline{Q_2}\), and the
complete row-2 trace belongs to \(\overline{Q_1}\).  Thus both traces
are retained in \(C_\tau\), including polygonal breakpoints, and the
genuine lower crossings give the exact active-section inequalities
\[
\ell_{0i}\leq s\ell_{2i}\qquad(i=1,2).
\]
In row \(i=1,2\), the positive \(Q_i\)-tail alone also forces
\[
\left|H_{12}\cap\{f_i\leq0\}\right|
>
\frac14\left(q_i+\frac{2p}{\Delta}\right).
\]
Hence the branch is empty whenever
\[
q_i+\frac{2p}{\Delta}\geq4U_i
\]
for either row.  The full diagonal-rail formula also gives a precise
retained-\(Q_{12}\) versus unretained-\(Q_{12}\)-bulge alternative.
Thus every survivor of the old hard interval must additionally have
both small diagonal-rail bounds, a quantitatively large
\(Q_{12}\setminus C_\tau\) bulge whenever the displayed threshold is
positive, and complete retention of both crossing traces.  The first
datum still not controlled by the old maximum-chord interval is the
location and size of the active \(P\)-sections relative to the
canonical cuts, not loss of the \(A_2\)-trace.
author: mp_r393_retained_bulge_dichotomy
proof:
We first prove the diagonal-rail formula.  Fix
\(i\in\{1,2\}\) and \(x\in X_i\).  By (8)-(9),
\[
0\leq\frac{x}{s}<1<\beta_i.
\tag{22}
\]
For
\[
\frac{x}{s}\leq t\leq\beta_i,
\qquad
u=x-st,
\tag{23}
\]
one has \(u\leq0\), \(t\in T_i\), and \(u+st=x\in X_i\).
In the notation of the exact two-rail identity in accepted fact
`cb3cba490b10885c`, choose the two selectors equal:
\[
t_-(u)=t_+(u)=\frac{x-u}{s}.
\tag{24}
\]
The corresponding integrand is
\[
\Phi_i(u;t_-(u),t_+(u))
=w_i^P(x)+s\,w_i^C\!\left(\frac{x-u}{s}\right)
\geq0.
\tag{25}
\]
Integrating (25) on \(x-s\beta_i\leq u\leq0\) and using
\(du=-s\,dt\), accepted fact `cb3cba490b10885c` gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left|H_{12}\cap\{f_i\leq0\}\right|
&\geq\frac14
\left[
(s\beta_i-x)w_i^P(x)
+s^2\int_{x/s}^{\beta_i}w_i^C(t)\,dt
\right]\\
&=\frac14\mathcal D_i(x).
\end{aligned}
\tag{26}
\]
Taking the supremum proves the first inequality in (11).

Every strict point of \(Q_i\) has
\[
\tau_i>1,
\tag{27}
\]
because its other two \(\tau\)-coordinates are negative and the three
coordinates sum to one.  Thus (27) proves (8), and the whole cell
\(Q_i\) lies in the tail \(\{\tau_i\geq x/s\}\) occurring in
(10).  The second term of (10) is therefore at least \(q_i\):
\[
s^2\int_{x/s}^{\beta_i}w_i^C(t)\,dt\geq q_i.
\tag{28}
\]
Also
\[
p=\int_{X_i}w_i^P(x)\,dx,
\qquad
|X_i|\leq1.
\tag{29}
\]
The nonnegative function
\[
g_i(x)=(s\beta_i-x)w_i^P(x)
\]
satisfies
\[
\begin{aligned}
\max_{x\in X_i}g_i(x)
&\geq\frac1{|X_i|}\int_{X_i}g_i(x)\,dx\\
&\geq\int_{X_i}g_i(x)\,dx\\
&\geq(s\beta_i-1)p.
\end{aligned}
\tag{30}
\]
Choose a maximizer in (30) and use (28) at that same section.  This
proves the second inequality in (11).  Since \(\beta_i>1\) and
\(s-1=2/\Delta\), the last inequality in (11) is strict.

Accepted fact `3c17eb0b21eeb63c` gives
\[
H_{12}\subseteq K,\qquad
\left|K\cap\{f_i\leq0\}\right|<U_i.
\tag{31}
\]
Thus (12) and (11) contradict (31), proving the new scalar gate and
its necessary reverse (13).

For (15), set \(x=0\) in (26).  Both
\(\overline{Q_1}^{\,\tau}\) and
\(\overline{Q_2}^{\,\tau}\) lie in \(\{\tau_3\leq0\}\), hence so
does \(C_\tau\).  Convexity of \(A_{2,\tau}\) gives
\(C_\tau\subseteq A_{2,\tau}\).  Up to null coordinate lines,
\[
C_\tau\cap\{\tau_1\geq0\}
=Q_1^\tau\mathbin{\dot\cup}
\left(C_\tau\cap Q_{12}^\tau\right),
\tag{32}
\]
and symmetrically for row \(2\).  Therefore
\[
s^2\int_0^{\beta_i}w_i^C(t)\,dt=q_i+\gamma_C.
\tag{33}
\]
Equations (26) and (33) prove (15).  Combining (15) with (31) in
both rows gives (16).  Since \(C_\tau\subseteq A_{2,\tau}\), the
retained part of \(Q_{12}\) has area exactly \(\gamma_C\), while the
whole cell has area \(q_{12}\).  Subtraction proves (17).

It remains to prove the full-trace retention.  Suppose first that
\[
z\in A_{2,\tau}\cap\{\tau_1=0\}
\quad\hbox{and}\quad
\tau_2(z)<1.
\tag{34}
\]
Choose an interior point \(y\) of the positive-area cell \(Q_2\).
Then
\[
\tau_1(y)<0,\qquad\tau_2(y)>0,\qquad\tau_3(y)<0.
\tag{35}
\]
For every sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), the point
\[
z_\varepsilon=(1-\varepsilon)z+\varepsilon y
\]
belongs to \(\operatorname{int}A_{2,\tau}\): a strict convex
combination of a point of a convex body with one of its interior
points is interior.

If \(0\leq\tau_2(z)<1\), then, for sufficiently small
\(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
\tau_1(z_\varepsilon)<0,\qquad
\tau_2(z_\varepsilon)>0,\qquad
\tau_3(z_\varepsilon)>0.
\]
Thus \(z_\varepsilon\) lies in the unsupported strict cell \(Q_{23}\).
Because it is an interior point of \(A_{2,\tau}\), a small ball around
it gives \(q_{23}>0\), contradicting the exact support
\(\{123,1,2,12\}\).  If \(\tau_2(z)<0\), then for small
\(\varepsilon\) one instead has
\[
\tau_1(z_\varepsilon)<0,\qquad
\tau_2(z_\varepsilon)<0,\qquad
\tau_3(z_\varepsilon)>0,
\]
which gives the same contradiction in the unsupported strict cell
\(Q_3\).  Therefore every point of the row-1 section has
\(\tau_2\geq1\), proving the first inclusion in (18a).  Its remaining
inclusions follow from the exact sign convention.  Interchanging
indices \(1,2\) and using an interior point of \(Q_1\) proves (18b).
Since \(C_\tau\subseteq A_{2,\tau}\), the asserted section equalities
follow as well.

We next derive the active chord comparison.  Increase the row-\(i\)
endpoint level from \(L_i\) to \(L_i+\eta\).  In the coordinates (3),
the \(A_0\)-cap gains the strip
\[
0<r_i\leq\frac{\eta}{\Delta},
\]
whereas the \(A_2\)-cap loses the strip
\[
0\leq\tau_i<\frac{\eta}{\Delta+2}.
\]
Both active lines cross the interiors of the endpoint bodies: the
finite-interior condition does this for \(A_0\), and the positive
cells \(Q_1,Q_2\) do it for \(A_2\).  Polygonal chord continuity and
Cavalieri integration therefore give the right first-order change
\[
\frac{\eta}{\Delta}
\left(\ell_{0i}-s\ell_{2i}\right)+o(\eta).
\tag{36}
\]
At a genuine lower crossing there are values arbitrarily close on
the right where the endpoint-cap sum is smaller than its crossing
value.  Equation (36) forces
\[
\ell_{0i}\leq s\ell_{2i}.
\tag{37}
\]
The section of \(P\) is contained in the full section of \(A_0\), so
\(\ell_i\leq\ell_{0i}\).  This proves (19), including equality at a
polygonal breakpoint.

Finally, the section-length function \(w_i^C\) is concave on its
projection interval.  For \(0\leq t\leq\beta_i\),
\[
w_i^C(t)\geq
\left(1-\frac{t}{\beta_i}\right)w_i^C(0),
\]
because the terminal section length is nonnegative.  Integrating,
using (33), and then using (19), gives
\[
q_i+\gamma_C
=s^2\int_0^{\beta_i}w_i^C(t)\,dt
\geq\frac{s^2\beta_i}{2}\ell_{2i}
\geq\frac{s\beta_i}{2}\ell_i.
\]
This proves (20), and its substitution in (15) proves (21).

The maximum-chord inequalities and hard interval in accepted fact
`3c17eb0b21eeb63c` use only section maxima and total areas.  Equations
(10), (16), and (19) show the extra data now isolated: the active
\(P\)-section locations and the retained \(Q_{12}\) tail profile.
Equations (18a)-(18b) show that an unretained \(Q_{123}\)-side
crossing trace is not an admissible escape.  No step above assumes
constant chords or that an active cut avoids a polygonal breakpoint.
statement:
Use all hypotheses and notation of accepted fact
`3c17eb0b21eeb63c`.  In particular,
\[
p=|P_\varnothing|>0,\qquad
q_1,q_2,q_{12},q_{123}>0,
\]
\[
M=|A_0|,\qquad m=|A_2|,\qquad
\kappa=|K|<M+m,
\]
and
\[
U_i=\frac{4(M+m)}9-u_i-v_i
\qquad(i=1,2).
\tag{1}
\]
Assume in addition that all three displayed endpoint levels are the
genuine lower crossings in the canonical subgoal.
Put
\[
\Delta=-1-(L_1+L_2+L_3)>2,
\qquad
s=\frac{\Delta+2}{\Delta}=1+\frac2\Delta,
\tag{2}
\]
and use the normalized affine coordinates
\[
r_i=\frac{f_i-L_i}{\Delta},\qquad
\tau_i=-\frac{f_i+L_i}{\Delta+2},\qquad
\lambda_i=-\frac{L_i}{\Delta}.
\tag{3}
\]
Then
\[
\sum_i r_i=\sum_i\tau_i=1,\qquad
r_i=2\lambda_i-s\tau_i.
\tag{4}
\]
Apply one common affine area normalization so that the
\((r_1,r_2)\)-coordinate area is the area used below.  Consequently,
an area computed in the \(\tau\)-plane is multiplied by \(s^2\).

Let
\[
P=\overline{P_\varnothing}
\]
in the \(r\)-plane, let \(A_{2,\tau}\) be the \(\tau\)-image of
\(A_2\), and put
\[
C_\tau=
\operatorname{conv}\bigl(
\overline{Q_1}^{\,\tau}\cup
\overline{Q_2}^{\,\tau}\bigr),
\qquad
H_{12}=\frac12(P+2\lambda-sC_\tau).
\tag{5}
\]
For \(i=1,2\), choose either other barycentric coordinate as a
transverse area coordinate.  Write the nonempty sections as
\[
P_{i,x}=[A_i^P(x),B_i^P(x)]
\quad(x\in X_i),
\]
\[
(C_\tau)_{i,t}=[L_i^C(t),R_i^C(t)]
\quad(t\in T_i),
\tag{6}
\]
and put
\[
w_i^P(x)=B_i^P(x)-A_i^P(x),\qquad
w_i^C(t)=R_i^C(t)-L_i^C(t),
\qquad
\beta_i=\max T_i.
\tag{7}
\]
The positive cell \(Q_i\) gives
\[
\beta_i>1,
\tag{8}
\]
while \(P\) lies in the standard \(r\)-simplex, so
\[
X_i\subseteq[0,1].
\tag{9}
\]

For every \(x\in X_i\), define the diagonal-rail quantity
\[
\mathcal D_i(x)=
(s\beta_i-x)w_i^P(x)
+s^2\int_{x/s}^{\beta_i}w_i^C(t)\,dt.
\tag{10}
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{\quad
\left|H_{12}\cap\{f_i\leq0\}\right|
\geq\frac14\sup_{x\in X_i}\mathcal D_i(x)
\geq
\frac14\bigl((s\beta_i-1)p+q_i\bigr)
>
\frac14\left(q_i+\frac{2p}{\Delta}\right).
\quad}
\tag{11}
\]
Consequently either scalar condition
\[
\boxed{\quad
q_i+\frac{2p}{\Delta}\geq4U_i
\quad}
\tag{12}
\]
excludes the canonical branch.  Every survivor must satisfy
\[
4U_i>q_i+\frac{2p}{\Delta}
\qquad(i=1,2).
\tag{13}
\]
This is a nonempty additional closing chamber beyond merely requiring
the maximum-chord ratios to lie in the interval of accepted fact
`3c17eb0b21eeb63c`.

There is a sharper retained-\(Q_{12}\) consequence when the active
face of \(P\) is present.  Define
\[
\gamma_C=
s^2\left|
C_\tau\cap
\{\tau_1\geq0,\ \tau_2\geq0,\ \tau_3\leq0\}
\right|_\tau.
\tag{14}
\]
Then \(0\leq\gamma_C\leq q_{12}\), and, whenever
\(0\in X_i\), putting
\[
\ell_i=w_i^P(0)
\]
gives
\[
\boxed{\quad
\left|H_{12}\cap\{f_i\leq0\}\right|
\geq
\frac14\bigl(s\beta_i\ell_i+q_i+\gamma_C\bigr).
\quad}
\tag{15}
\]
If \(0\in X_1\cap X_2\), every survivor therefore obeys
\[
\gamma_C<
B:=\min_{i=1,2}
\{4U_i-s\beta_i\ell_i-q_i\},
\tag{16}
\]
and hence the unretained doubleton bulge satisfies
\[
\boxed{\quad
s^2\left|Q_{12}^{\tau}\setminus C_\tau\right|_\tau
=q_{12}-\gamma_C
>q_{12}-B.
\quad}
\tag{17}
\]
In particular, if \(B<q_{12}\), (17) is a strictly positive,
separately quantified missing-bulge requirement.

The two complete active \(A_2\)-traces are in fact retained:
\[
\boxed{\quad
A_{2,\tau}\cap\{\tau_1=0\}
\subseteq\{\tau_2\geq1,\ \tau_3\leq0\}
\subseteq\overline{Q_2}^{\,\tau}\subseteq C_\tau,
\quad}
\tag{18a}
\]
\[
\boxed{\quad
A_{2,\tau}\cap\{\tau_2=0\}
\subseteq\{\tau_1\geq1,\ \tau_3\leq0\}
\subseteq\overline{Q_1}^{\,\tau}\subseteq C_\tau.
\quad}
\tag{18b}
\]
Because \(C_\tau\subseteq A_{2,\tau}\), these inclusions are
equalities between the full \(A_2\)-section and the corresponding
\(C_\tau\)-section.

Let \(\ell_{0i}\) be the full \(r\)-coordinate chord length of
\(A_0\cap\{r_i=0\}\), and put
\[
\ell_{2i}=w_i^C(0).
\]
Whenever \(0\in X_i\), one has
\[
\boxed{\quad
\ell_i\leq\ell_{0i}\leq s\ell_{2i}.
\quad}
\tag{19}
\]
Moreover, concavity of the \(C_\tau\)-section profile gives
\[
q_i+\gamma_C
\geq\frac{s^2\beta_i}{2}\ell_{2i}
\geq\frac{s\beta_i}{2}\ell_i,
\tag{20}
\]
and hence (15) also implies
\[
\left|H_{12}\cap\{f_i\leq0\}\right|
\geq\frac{3s\beta_i\ell_i}{8}.
\tag{21}
\]
